This is a story about parallel lines and dimensions that never intersect. It explores the existential and metaphysical gaps between people and circumstances that make them invisible to one another. Every day, we encounter thousands of people, but most of them remain transparent to us because they exist outside our social bubble.

This narrative serves as a meditation on longing, fragmentation, and the silent architecture of separation that shapes human experience. The sense of separation in this work is enhanced by the layering that is filtered through colour theory.

Margaret is a Montreal-based artist whose work is a vibrant exploration of colour, movement, and emotion. Originally trained as a chef, she spent 15 years in the culinary world before fully committing to her artistic practice in 2016. Painting in acrylic, she embraces both the structured and spontaneous, creating collections that evolve in response—and sometimes in opposition—to one another.

Her work is deeply intuitive, guided by the emotional energy she channels onto the canvas. Through layered textures, bold contrasts, and expressive brushwork, Margaret transforms feelings into visual compositions, allowing rage to become beautiful, sadness to provide comfort, and joy to shine untarnished. Her collections reflect this journey, from the serene, muted tones of Serenity to the dynamic tension of Borders Not Limits and the raw energy of Wild.

Beyond technique, Margaret’s practice is rooted in personal expansion. A Reiki Grand Master, she draws inspiration from the emotional awakenings of women reclaiming their voices, as well as her own journey toward self-acceptance. Her paintings invite viewers to embrace the power of their emotions, recognizing the ever-changing flow of feeling as a force of transformation.

Margaret lives and creates in Montreal, Canada, and occasionally in Kalamazoo, Michigan.

Zahara is an ode to motherhood and the identity that continues to grow within it. This pregnant Black woman stands in quiet power, surrounded by yellow daisies that echo her fertility, resilience, and personal bloom. The thick butter-yellow lines behind her evoke the presence of her ancestors, grounding her as she carries the future. More than a mother, she remains whole — rooted, evolving, and deeply herself.

About the collection — My Memory Garden
A series inspired by childhood memories and maternal heritage. Each portrait celebrates imperfect, human, soft-yet-strong women. The repeated background lines symbolize memory, legacy, and the stories carried across generations.

URBAN WALLPAPERS is a series painted on ornamental tapestry wallpaper—originally designed to be pasted in the streets. This medium creates a bridge between my street work and my gallery pieces on carpet, while keeping the decorative aesthetic at the core of my practice.

The wallpapers, sourced from France, offer a fresh surface where intricate patterns meet bold portraiture. Some works are hand-painted, others torn, embossed, or detailed in gold—each one unique, just like us. This series brings the richness and texture of my rug art into a smaller, more intimate format, giving collectors a one-of-a-kind piece with depth, detail, and character.

This series of works explores the energy, resilience, and credibility that street hawkers embody in their daily practices. I am particularly drawn to how they arrange goods to maximize visual appeal and capture attention. The deliberate organization of products and the interplay of colours transform their displays into forms of artistic expression. By documenting these practices, my work seeks to highlight the creativity, resourcefulness, and aesthetic dimensions embedded within this everyday economic activity.

  • Photography print
  • Limited edition of 20
  • Unframed
This series of works explores the energy, resilience, and credibility that street hawkers embody in their daily practices. I am particularly drawn to how they arrange goods to maximize visual appeal and capture attention. The deliberate organization of products and the interplay of colours transform their displays into forms of artistic expression. By documenting these practices, my work seeks to highlight the creativity, resourcefulness, and aesthetic dimensions embedded within this everyday economic activity.

Lane radiates clarity and calm. Her soft blond hair and crystalline blue eyes contrast gently with the visible texture of the canvas beneath her, grounding her in truth. Dusk-toned lines wrap around her like a slow exhale, offering a moment of serenity in motion.

Each piece in this series is part of an intimate collection of 12x16” oil-on-canvas portraits celebrating feminine diversity and inner power. Painted with expressive brushwork and refined detail, these works are a tribute to multicultural beauty, self-acceptance, and the richness of human experience. Custom framed in solid Cherrywood, they’re created with both new and seasoned collectors in mind — offering connection, reflection, and a moment of stillness in our ever-moving world.

12” x 16” oil on canvas, custom framed in Cherrywood, 2025.

This is part of the Trashion Couture collection.

  • Photography print
  • Limited edition of 10
  • Unframed
I have spent the last few years collecting trash that I find on my travels, who’s shape, after enduring the elements, reminds me of pieces of clothing. I pair these items with carefully selected images that I cut out of recycled magazines. I believe “trashion,” be it vegetable waste couture from a compost collection, or plastic fancy work from a candy bar wrapper, is an art form of today. Once overlooked, it has become my unexpected canvas. Through this work, I reflect on our relationship with materiality, excess and the fleeting nature of both the things we cherish and those we discard, while at the same time, urging a reconsideration of our consumption habits and the true cost of fleeting beauty.
- Lora Moore

column3:
This powerful feminist piece embodies liberation from the gaze of others and the reclamation of autonomy. Inspired by the 1786 Tignon Law—which sought to suppress Black women’s self-expression through mandated head coverings—the artwork reinterprets this history as a symbol of beauty, resilience, and defiance.

Echoing the spirit of Portrait de Madeleine (often called "the Black Mona Lisa of the Louvre" and featured in Beyoncé and Jay-Z’s Apeshit video), the painting reclaims visibility and agency, paying tribute to women who transform oppression into elegance.

The background’s color palette draws from classic African textile patterns, celebrating cultural heritage and linking past and present through fabric, self-expression, and creativity.

column3: "I am me in a hundred ways and I am creating space for each. A space with friends, a space in solitude. The balance of being all of myself felt overwhelming at first but then I realized it was more about relaxing into myself. It has become about recognizing those places where is it easy, recognizing the people who see me, and letting my voice speak more of the words within my heart. I have learned to gather spaces that I can visit when I need the silence, spaces for celebrating, and spaces for loving this life. It is a slow process, a deliberate one, a carefully curated journey to allowing that inner me to feel safe in the world."

column3:
"We were discussing where we would each go to revive our souls. To get away but also restore and reignite our inner fire. I found it interesting that the locations were different, but they were all outside. All of us wanted to reconnect in some way with nature, whether the mountains or the water, the forest or a vast open prairie.

I have learned since I began painting how deeply important the water is to me. That being on the beach, warming my toes in the sand, feeling the movement of the waves, that is my place. It takes my many moods and brings comfort to each one."

column3:
Everything has beauty, but not everyone sees it. – Confucius

"It took some time to learn how to slow down. My kids taught me the first steps when they were very little, when I had little sleep and sat in wonder of their tiny fingers and toes.  Practicing meditation gave me another step along the path as I learned that I could be quiet in my mind and see more of what was sharing the room with me. The pandemic moved me further along the way, as I had many days of nothing to do.

I walked or biked along the same streets and paths, yet there was always something new. The shadows fell in different piles, a kite caught in a tree whispered for me to look up at it waving about, or a crane landing on the river. Nature is very good at helping us to pay attention. And now I look to find beauty indoors as well, in people, in moments, and in treasures I collected and then forgot.  What a gift it is that in every moment there is something extraordinary to witness, if we slow down, if we take the time to see it."

column3: This artwork celebrates the rarity and uniqueness of existence by portraying a muse grounded in her maternal lineage. The intricate lines in the background symbolize the one-in-four-hundred-trillion chance of being born as you. Each line, painted with deep reverence, represents generations of women giving life to one another. This piece invites viewers to reflect on their journey, celebrating the profound beauty of individuality and the strength of ancestral connections. "One in Four Hundred Trillion" serves as a daily reminder of the extraordinary miracle of life and the importance of honoring those who came before us.

column3: This work celebrates beauty in difference by depicting a muse living with vitiligo, which depigments the skin. The muse's eyes, a true mirror of her soul, are brought to the fore with particular intensity. At the same time, the facial features become more expressive as they move away from the eyes, reminiscent of Rubens' studies. The background lines, dark at the base and gradually lightening, symbolize the muse's loss of pigmentation. This work invites us to anchor ourselves in the present moment and celebrate diversity with patience and serenity.

column3: "Patience Is Powerful” is an evocative oil on canvas portrait inspired by the artist's youngest daughter, Marianne. This piece symbolizes a young adult’s eagerness to grow and the importance of embracing each life stage. Reflecting Marianne’s features, it captures the bittersweet passage of time. The muse, reminiscent of Botticelli’s Venus, represents modern female empowerment and transcends traditional objectification. Using a colour palette echoing Botticelli, the variations in tones symbolize the ebb and flow of life’s events. This artwork invites viewers to witness their own beauty and strength through the prism of art.

column3:
Inspired by the mystical symbolism of "as above, so below", this artwork explores the coexistence between our facade and our shadows. The double portrait in mirror juxtaposes an upper figure embodying the perfection we choose to show the world, an image shaped to meet societal expectations.

In contrast, the lower figure is more raw, more chaotic, with a small heart tattoo beneath the eye. It reveals our hidden, unconscious, and vulnerable emotions, representing the shadowed aspects of our personality—less refined, more authentic.

The composition evokes the form of a playing card, emphasizing the idea that each woman reigns over her life. Inspired by the myth of Lilith, this piece becomes a tribute to feminine power, liberation from imposed roles, and the assertion of personal agency. Through this duality, the artist invites viewers to embrace all facets of their identity, celebrating self-acceptance and the reconciliation of light and darkness. This mystical and modern work challenges how our shadows shape our true being and destiny.
